hypothesis: A fixed lookup library of completed historical pitcher-season/count/hand prototypes can recover local nonlinear control behavior that global trees and exact categorical shrinkage miss. Retrieval uses only the current row's official state vector and a frozen history library, so every evaluation/test row is predicted independently.

novelty_audit.prior_group_rates: V3 history groups and V4/V5 residual tables used exact categorical tables. They did not search continuous current-state neighborhoods across pitchers.
novelty_audit.prior_tabr: The only TabR run was a 50k-row two-epoch CPU smoke on 2024. It was not a fixed, auditable temporal prototype estimator and was never source-validated.
novelty_audit.prior_catboost: CatBoost partitions continuous features globally; this candidate performs explicit local kernel retrieval over completed-history prototypes.

prototype.history_rule: season strictly before target season; R rows only
numeric_state: official previous 1/3/5 game success and middle rates
month, inning, outs, runner count, score differential and leverage
prototype.scaling: history-prototype median and IQR/1.349, with standard-deviation fallback; frozen per target fold
prototype.distance: exact L2 by FAISS IndexFlatL2 inside a fixed count-and-hand bucket
prototype.neighbor_weight: inverse (1 + Euclidean distance) times sqrt(min(prototype rows, 256))

selection_order: maximize minimum full-score gain over 2020 and 2021
maximize minimum R-score gain over 2020 and 2021
prefer fewer neighbors, smaller amplitude and smaller parent gamma

source_protocol.on_fail: Close prototype retrieval without reading 2022+ labels.
source_protocol.on_pass: Freeze mode, k, amplitudes and all library construction before untouched 2022/2023 development.
